response: Yes, there is awareness of pharmaceutical expenditure in the reformed primary care system. In fact, one of the key goals of primary care reform is to optimize pharmaceutical utilization and contain costs. Many countries have implemented various measures to monitor and manage pharmaceutical expenditure, such as electronic prescribing, medication therapy management, and cost-sharing mechanisms. Additionally, healthcare providers and policymakers are increasingly recognizing the importance of pharmaceutical expenditure management in primary care, and are working to improve awareness and education among patients, providers, and other stakeholders.
